summary.text: Saint Philaret was Metropolitan of Moscow, a theological teacher, preacher, and catechism writer whose work shaped religious education in nineteenth-century Russia.

blocks.text: Born in Kolomna in 1782, he received the baptismal name Basil. His father was a clergyman. He studied in seminaries where Latin predominated, became a monk in 1808, and later taught theology in Saint Petersburg.

blocks.text: Consecrated bishop in 1817, he became Metropolitan of Moscow in 1826. He supported teaching theology in Russian and translating Scripture into contemporary Russian. He also defended monastic elders and helped the publication of patristic books.

blocks.text: Saint Philaret died on November 19, 1867, after celebrating his final Divine Liturgy that day. He was buried at the Trinity Lavra. The life does not describe martyrdom.

blocks.text: His catechism appeared in 1823. Its explanations of Christian doctrine became influential beyond Russia. His preaching and educational work connect his biography directly with the catechetical material used in Learn.
